Interface CausalConsumer<K,V>

Type Parameters:
K - the record key type
V - the record value type
All Superinterfaces:
AutoCloseable, Closeable
public interface CausalConsumer<K,V> extends Closeable
A high-level Kafka consumer that delivers records in causal order.

A CausalConsumer wraps a Kafka Streams topology to provide causal ordering across one or more topics. Records whose CausalDependencies dependencies are not yet satisfied by the current frontier are held in an internal buffer; once the frontier catches up, buffered records are released and returned in subsequent poll(Duration) calls.

Usage

try (CausalConsumer<String, Order> consumer = CausalConsumers.<String, Order>builder(
        List.of("prices", "orders"),
        CausalBufferPolicy.forwardUnsafe(CausalBufferLimit.ofDuration(Duration.ofSeconds(30))),
        Map.of(),
        streamsConfig).build()) {

    ConsumerRecords<String, Order> records = consumer.poll(Duration.ofMillis(200));
    CausalDependencies frontier = consumer.frontier(); // pass to a CausalProducer when producing
}

Thread safety

Like Kafka's own Consumer, poll(Duration) is intended to be driven by a single thread. Polling concurrently from several threads does not corrupt the consumer, but it splits the causally-ordered record stream across those threads — so each thread sees only a subset, defeating the ordering guarantee this consumer exists to provide. Unlike Kafka's consumer, this is not detected or rejected; it is simply the caller's responsibility.

frontier() is safe to call from any thread, concurrently with poll and with the internal stream threads. close() is safe to call from a thread other than the poller, but it does not interrupt a poll already blocked waiting for records — there is no wakeup(); the in-flight poll simply returns empty once its timeout elapses.

  • Method Details

    • poll

      org.apache.kafka.clients.consumer.ConsumerRecords<K,V> poll(Duration timeout)
      Polls for records whose causal dependencies are satisfied.

      Records with unsatisfied dependencies remain buffered until the frontier catches up or the configured CausalBufferLimit fires.

      Delivery guarantee

      Records are delivered at-least-once: admitted records are written to an internal Kafka outbox topic before being returned here, so they survive a crash and will be re-delivered on restart. For exactly-once delivery, set processing.guarantee=exactly_once_v2 in the streamsConfig passed to CausalConsumers; the internal outbox consumer already reads with isolation.level=read_committed, so no additional configuration is needed.
      Parameters:
      timeout - the maximum time to block waiting for records; must not be null
      Returns:
      records ready for processing; never null, may be empty

    • frontier

      CausalFrontier frontier()
      Returns the current causal frontier — the highest offset seen on each partition, i.e. everything this consumer has processed so far.

      Call CausalFrontier.toDependencies() to convert to a CausalDependencies for passing to CausalProducer.send(ProducerRecord) or for cross-service propagation. To instead read the causal context of one specific consumed message — the upstream producer's dependencies — use CausalDependencies.fromRecord(org.apache.kafka.clients.consumer.ConsumerRecord).

      Returns:
      the current CausalFrontier; never null
